crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Personalised Wealth Advice
children.blurb: Personalised wealth advice covers systems that tailor portfolio recommendations to an individual's goals, time horizon, tax position and tolerance for loss, rather than selling one model portfolio to everyone.

children.name: Portfolio Optimisation Beyond Mean and Variance
children.blurb: Portfolio optimisation beyond mean and variance covers the methods used to choose asset weights when the classic trade-off between expected return and variance is judged too narrow.

children.name: Tail Risk Hedging
children.blurb: Tail risk hedging covers the positions and instruments a portfolio holds specifically to pay off during rare, severe market moves rather than during ordinary trading.

children.name: Sustainability Factors in Portfolios
children.blurb: Sustainability factors in portfolios are the environmental, social and governance characteristics that an investor measures, weights and reports alongside financial ones.

children.name: Pricing Illiquid Assets
children.blurb: Pricing illiquid assets covers the valuation of holdings that do not trade on a public market, such as private company stakes, real estate, private credit, and stakes in funds that themselves hold hard to sell positions.

sections.body: Portfolio construction is the work of deciding what a person or institution should hold, in what amounts, and why. Artificial intelligence is now used to build and adjust those holdings from data about markets, goals, constraints and taxes. In personalised wealth advice, systems draft allocation suggestions and rebalancing plans that a human adviser reviews. In optimisation, machine learning estimates expected returns and correlations where the classical mean and variance approach is too crude. In tail risk hedging, models look for signals that precede large losses and propose hedges. In sustainability factors, AI reads company disclosures and news to score environmental and social exposure. In pricing illiquid assets, models infer values for holdings that rarely trade.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The field is partly solved and partly not. Optimisation and rebalancing are well understood, and AI mainly improves the inputs and the speed of solving. Personalised advice works at scale for straightforward goals, but it struggles when a household has unusual income, debt or family obligations. Tail risk hedging remains the hardest part, because the events being hedged are rare and the historical record is thin, so models often fit noise. Sustainability scoring is improving but depends on inconsistent disclosure and judgement calls about what counts. Pricing illiquid assets is possible for some private credit and real estate, yet the estimates carry wide uncertainty and can be slow to reflect new information. Across all of it, the honest limit is that past data does not guarantee future behaviour, and no model removes the need for human oversight.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages here form a sequence from broad advice to narrow technical problems. Personalised Wealth Advice is the entry point, covering how goals, risk tolerance and constraints become a suggested portfolio. Portfolio Optimisation Beyond Mean and Variance goes deeper into the mathematics, for readers who want to know how AI changes the objective being solved. Tail Risk Hedging is the defensive counterpart, focused on protecting against extreme losses rather than improving average returns. Sustainability Factors in Portfolios sits alongside these, showing how non financial preferences are measured and inserted into the construction process. Pricing Illiquid Assets is the foundation page, because you cannot optimise or hedge what you cannot value. Read together, they show a pipeline: value the holdings, choose the mix, protect the downside, and align the result with the investor's stated aims.
